# Wetland samples

Now we go on to create the actual samples for ANO våtmark (wetlands), using `spaceR::nested_balanced_samples`.

We updated the sample in may 2026.

```{r setup_sample}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| error: false
library(tidyverse)
library(dbplyr)
library(DBI)
library(RPostgres)
library(dm)
#detach("package:spaceR", unload=TRUE)
#Sys.unsetenv("GITHUB_PAT")
#Sys.unsetenv("GITHUB_TOKEN")
#remotes::install_github("NINAnor/spaceR", force = T)
library(spaceR)
#?nested_balanced

```

## Get and prepare sampling frame
First we need to fetch the sampling frame from the database.
```{r viewData}
#| include: true
#| eval: true
con <- DBI::dbConnect(drv = RPostgres::Postgres(), host = "t2lippgsql03", dbname = "ano_moduler")

pop <- dplyr::tbl(con, dbplyr::in_schema("sampling_frames", "samplingframe_vaatmark_2026")) |>
  dplyr::collect()

# helper to get a small subset of the data for testing
small <- function(data = pop) data |>  slice_sample(n = 10000)
```

This dataset (sampling frame) is `r nrow(pop)` long. @tbl-sf show just the first ten rows. We have two spreading variables: an easting `ost`, a northing `nord`. We also have sampling unit ID's in `ssbid`, and two auxiliary variable for balancing: `mean_slope` and `abi`. The stratification variable is called `region_ko` or `region_number`. We also need to create an `area` variable based on the sum of `r_hav` and `r_ferskvann`. 

```{r tbl-sf}
#| include: true
pop |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  DT::datatable()
```

```{r datacheck}
#| eval: false
#| include: false
summary(pop$r_ferskvann)
summary(pop$r_hav)
wet_small <- small(pop)
dotchart(wet_small$r_ferskvann)
dotchart(wet_small$r_hav)
dotchart(wet_small$centroid_x)
dotchart(wet_small$centroid_y)
dotchart(wet_small$ost)
dotchart(wet_small$nord)

dotchart(wet_small$mean_slope)
dotchart(wet_small$abi)
hist(wet_small$abi)

```

```{r makeVars}
#| eval: true
pop <- pop |>
  rename(Northing = nord, Easting = ost) |>
  mutate(
    area = 100 - r_hav - r_ferskvann,
    stratum = as.character(region_number)
  )
```

There is one or a few cases of negative areas. I will just set those to be zeros.
```{r}
#| eval: true
# min(pop$area) #negative
# max(pop$area) #OK
pop <- pop |>
  mutate(area = case_when(
    area < 0 ~ 0,
    .default = area
  ))
wet_small <- small(pop)

```


```{r tbl-n}
#| eval: true
#| tbl-cap: 'Number of population units (SSB500 squares) in each strata.'
pop |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(n = n())
```

There is a potnetial issue with `abi` that we have false zero values, because we 
see that there are quite some cases where ABI is zero and r_bebygd_samf is not zero.
Maybe this has a natural explanation, but I am not sure. 

```{r}
plot(wet_small$r_bebygd_samf, wet_small$abi)
```

I though that maybe this was an edge effect from water, but the plot below doesn't tell this.

```{r}
wet_small |>
  filter(abi == 0 & r_bebygd_samf > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(area)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(
    x = "Area that is land (%)",
    y = "Number of cells with ABI zero and r_bebygd_samf > 0"
  )
```

So I will have to ignore this potential issue for now. 


## Sample
First we subset the columns, and run a test on 10 000 rows.
```{r stripdata}
#| eval: true
pop <- pop |>
  select(
    ssbid,
    Easting,
    Northing,
    area,
    abi,
    mean_slope,
    stratum,
    geographic_region,
    fylk2016,
    fylk_navn,
    komm2016
  )

wet_small <- small()
```

```{r test}
#| eval: true
testRun <- spaceR::nested_balanced(
  samplingFrame = wet_small,
  n_seq = seq(50, 20, -10),
  id_col = "ssbid",
  stratum_col = "stratum",
  easting_col = "Easting",
  northing_col = "Northing",
  area_col = "area",
  xbal_formula = ~ abi + mean_slope -1,
  exclude_offset = 1e+09,
  return_dataframe = TRUE,
  out_name = "testSample"
)
```


The test went fine, with no errors. 

The returned object `testRun` which is a list of lists. 
```{r testnames}
#| eval: true
names(testRun)
```

Then we try the same on the entire sampling population

```{r sampleAll}
#| eval: false
tictoc::tic()
wetlands <- spaceR::nested_balanced(
  samplingFrame = pop,
  n_seq = seq(1000, 10, -10),
  id_col = "ssbid",
  stratum_col = "stratum",
  easting_col = "Easting",
  northing_col = "Northing",
  area_col = "area",
  xbal_formula = ~ abi + mean_slope -1,
  exclude_offset = 1e+09,
  return_dataframe = FALSE,
  out_name = "wetlands1",
)
tictoc::toc()
# 1012.165 sec elapsed
#saveRDS(wetlands, "data/wetlands2026.rds")
```

Now I will combine all these lists of lists into something more manageable, like a dataframe.

```{r combinedata}
sample_names <- names(wetlands)
sample_sizes <- gsub("wetlands1_", "", sample_names) |> as.numeric()
all_ids <- wetlands$wetlands1_1000$ID

# Initialize empty matrix with NA
prob_matrix <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(all_ids), ncol = length(sample_names),
                      dimnames = list(all_ids, sample_sizes))

# Fill in probabilities where IDs occur
for (i in seq_along(wetlands)) {
  w <- wetlands[[i]]
  id_match <- match(w$ID, all_ids)
  prob_matrix[id_match, i] <- w$prob
}

# create column with IDs
prob_matrix <-  prob_matrix |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("ssbid") |>
  as_tibble()

# append aux data
prob_matrix <- pop |>
  right_join(prob_matrix, by = join_by(ssbid))

head(prob_matrix)
```

In the code below I check that the proportion of cells with >100% terrestrial area, stay stable after the initial pps, and the do. Compared to the full population,
we have reduced the proportion of sampling units that have less then 100 or 50% or area by approx. 9 and 71%, respectively.

```{r}
prob_matrix |>
  select(ssbid, area, "1000", "500", "100") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c("1000", "500", "100"),
               values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(prop_below_100 = mean(area < 100, na.rm=T),
            prop_below_50 = mean(area < 50, na.rm=T)) |>
  rbind(
    pop |>
  summarise(prop_below_100 = mean(area < 100, na.rm=T),
            prop_below_50 = mean(area < 50, na.rm=T)) |>
    add_column("name" = "Population", .before = 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

![](img/props.jpg)

## Evaluate balance

Here we should ideally evaluate the balance of the sample against a simple random sample, for example using `BalancedSampling::sb()`, but we don't have time to to this now unfortunately.

We can do a quick and dirty evaluation by filtering out cells with <100% terrestrial area, and sort of take out the pps factor. Then we get the mean for the balancing variables for each strata. We'll keep the analysis to strata 1.
```{r}
one <- pop |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), mean_abi = mean(abi)) |>
  add_column(sample = "all")

two <- prob_matrix |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), mean_abi = mean(abi)) |>
    add_column(sample = "1000")

three <- prob_matrix |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1 & !is.na(`500`)) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), mean_abi = mean(abi)) |>
    add_column(sample = "500")

four <- prob_matrix |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1 & !is.na(`100`)) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), mean_abi = mean(abi)) |>
    add_column(sample = "100")

five <- prob_matrix |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1 & !is.na(`50`)) |>
  group_by(stratum) |>
  summarise(mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), mean_abi = mean(abi)) |>
    add_column(sample = "50")
comb <- one |> bind_rows(two) |> bind_rows(three) |> bind_rows(four) |> bind_rows(five)
comb
```

It's not easy to say if this result is good or bad. At least there is no clear structure, for example that the mean decreases or increases as the samples get smaller. We can to add some simple random samples to compare.

```{r}
r1000 <- pop |>
  filter(area == 100 & stratum == 1) |>
  slice_sample(n = 1000)

r500 <- r1000 |> slice_sample(n = 500)
r100 <- r500 |> slice_sample(n = 100)
r50 <- r100 |> slice_sample(n = 50)

r1000 <- r1000 |>
  summarise(r_mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), r_mean_abi = mean(abi))

r500 <- r500 |>
  summarise(r_mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), r_mean_abi = mean(abi))

r100 <- r100 |>
  summarise(r_mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), r_mean_abi = mean(abi))

r50 <- r50 |>
  summarise(r_mean_slope = mean(mean_slope), r_mean_abi = mean(abi))

comb2 <- r1000 |>
  add_row(r_mean_slope = NA, r_mean_abi = NA, .before = 1) |>
  bind_rows(list(r500, r100, r50))

comb |>
  bind_cols(comb2) |>
  select(sample, mean_slope, r_mean_slope, mean_abi, r_mean_abi)
```

They are not very different. Maybe there is more of a founding bias for the SRS.
But I dont think this test is very robust. It should be replicated/bootstrapped, and the ppm makes it more difficult as well. 
At least the balanced samples are not very wrong. But I cant say for sure that they are more representative than SRS.

## Locations per region

How many sampling locations do we now get per geographic region for different total sampling sizes?
The sample size refers to the number of samples per stratum. 
So when n = 1000 we have 7000 samples nationally.

```{r}
prob_matrix %>=%
  filter(!is.na(`50`)) %>=%
  group_by(geographic_region) %>=%
  count(name = "n = 50") |>
  add_column(
    prob_matrix %>=%
      filter(!is.na(`60`)) %>=%
      group_by(geographic_region) %>=%
      count(name = "n = 60") %>=%
      ungroup() %>=%
      select("n = 60"),

    prob_matrix %>=%
      filter(!is.na(`70`)) %>=%
      group_by(geographic_region) %>=%
      count(name = "n = 70") %>=%
      ungroup() %>=%
      select("n = 70")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```


## Write to db

### Setup sample schema
This part sets up the schema, and is only done once

```{r}
schema_ur <- "CREATE SCHEMA samples"
dbSendQuery(con, schema_ur) 
```
Write queries to grant read only access to all.
```{r}
priv <- "ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA samples GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_ro"
priv2 <- "ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA samples GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_rw"
priv3 <- "ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA samples GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_admin"
priv4 <- "GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA samples  TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_admin"
priv5 <- "GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA samples  TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_rw"
priv6 <- "GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA samples  TO ag_pgsql_ano_moduler_ro"

dbSendStatement(con, priv)
dbSendStatement(con, priv2)
dbSendStatement(con, priv3)
dbSendStatement(con, priv4)
dbSendStatement(con, priv5)
dbSendStatement(con, priv6)
```

### Prepare and export

First I will try and make a sensible unique ID. 

```{r}
cols <- as.character(seq(1000, 10, -10))
prob_matrix2 <- prob_matrix %>%
  arrange(across(all_of(cols), ~ is.na(.))) %>%
  mutate(ano_vaatmark_2026_flateid = paste0("ID_", row_number()), .before=1)
```

```{r}
wetlands_db <- prob_matrix2 |>
  select(
    -Easting,
    -Northing,
    -area,
    -abi,
    -mean_slope,
    -stratum,
    -geographic_region,
    -fylk2016,
    -fylk_navn,
    -komm2016
  )

write_csv(wetlands_db, "data/wetland_samples_1000_2026.csv")
```
